gaps.explanation: 'Far too much information' is the correct intensifier pattern; 'far much' and 'far very' do not exist.

gaps.sentence: There is so ___ crime in this area that people are afraid.
gaps.explanation: 'So much' is used with uncountable nouns like crime; 'plenty' would need 'of'.

gaps.sentence: I haven't got ___ cash on me — I'll pay by card.
gaps.explanation: 'Any' is the normal quantifier in negative sentences; 'haven't got no cash' would be a double negative.

gaps.sentence: You can park on ___ side of the street.
gaps.hint: singular noun meaning 'this one or that one'
gaps.explanation: 'Either side' means one side or the other (both are allowed); 'both' would need the plural 'sides'.

gaps.sentence: If you walk instead of driving, you'll spend ___ on petrol.
gaps.explanation: 'Spend less' is the comparative with uncountable money; 'fewer' is for countable nouns.

gaps.sentence: This suitcase is ___ heavy to carry.
gaps.hint: adjective + this word + to-infinitive = impossible result
gaps.explanation: 'Too heavy to carry' means it is more heavy than possible; 'very' and 'so' cannot be followed directly by 'to'.

gaps.sentence: ___ of my two brothers work in banking.
gaps.explanation: 'Both of my two brothers work ...' is correct; 'all' and 'none' are not used for two.

gaps.sentence: There is ___ milk in the fridge — help yourself.
gaps.hint: affirmative statement; the invitation confirms it
gaps.explanation: 'Some milk' fits the affirmative statement and the invitation; 'no milk' would contradict 'help yourself'.
